newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends near day's peaks on trade coverin.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends near day's peaks on trade coverin.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended near the day's peaks in late trade short covering but prices remained locked in an tight range.

Traders said one big trade house emerged to buy on the May contract, sparking light short covering from some other players. Otherwise conditions were dull and involved routine day-to-day housekeeping.
News Ivorian cocoa arrivals reached 880,000 tonnes by February 23, against 920,000 at the same stage in the 1996 season, was within trade expectation and had no immediate influence.
"I don't think that (the Ivorian news) is the reason for it," said one.
By the close, May stood seven stg higher at 874 stg a tonne after a ceiling of 876. It hit a session low of 865.
Overall volume was 7,856 lots, centred on the March and May contracts.
Cocoa had been kept in a tight band for some time in view of a dearth of technical and fundamental inputs.
Traders said industry demand has been fairly subdued, making the market prone to any shortcovering.
But sterling has been firm against the French franc and German mark which has not been helpful.
"It's in a consolidation area. It will kick into life once its out of it. It's down to technicals and fundamentally, we would have to see a complete drying up of arrivals," said one.
Upside prospects were overshadowed by signs that West African arrivals may be shaping into another big harvest, although they were still likely to be smaller than last year's record.

Traders were looking for clues that the Ivorian main crop is beginning to taper off before the start of the mid-crop to conclude that the 1996/97 harvest may leave a large supply gap as forecast by several crop analysts.

"There is talk in the market that weekly arrivals have dried up to around 20,000 tonnes from 30,000. But I haven't seen much evidence of that. I think we have to wait another couple of weeks," said one trader.
The uncovered open interest on March showed a steep decline of 6,360 lots on Monday, reflecting the large cross done by Phibro against December.
Traders said the decline in the March open positions, to 9,213 lots, suggested that the expiry was likely to go smoothly.
